ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals (SDN) List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and Canadian domestic sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) pursuant to FINTRAC requirements, including 24/7 adverse media monitoring, source of wealth confirmation, and ongoing transaction surveillance for bonded trade counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Registry System) with NUANS name search clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names shall be in Latin script; non-English names must be transliterated into English or French. The name must contain the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or 'SRI'. No other corporate suffix is permitted. Names must be distinguishable from existing registrations and reserved names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the Director of Corporate Registry, Government of Alberta, within 30 days of the rejection, attaching a fresh NUANS report and supporting legal arguments. If the Director confirms the rejection, the applicant may file an application for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within 30 days of its decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office permitted for the statutory registered office address in Alberta, provided a registered agent service is engaged; however, the bonded trade business requires physical licensed premises for custody of goods under the Excise Act, 2001 and the Canada Border Services Agency regulations. A virtual address cannot substitute for operational bonded warehouse capacity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: more than 75% probability of at least one unannounced CBSA inspection of bonded premises within the first 12 months of commercial activity, with enhanced risk for alcohol and tobacco duty-bearing goods.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 12-22 (incorporation), ss 101-106 (registered office and records), and Part 14 (unlimited liability corporations); Alberta Regulation 276/2000, Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under Alberta Regulation 276/2000) together with Notice of Directors and Notice of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta ULC; no escrow account is required by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). Subscribers may pay capital into the corporation's operational bank account upon issuance, and any escrow arrangement will only be imposed by contract or as a condition of a licensed alcohol wholesaler bond facility.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) THE SUBSCRIPTIONS FOR THE ISSUED SHARES OF THE COMPANY SET FORTH IN THE SHARE SUBSCRIPTION LEDGER ARE ACCEPTED, AND SUCH SHARES ARE APPROVED FOR ISSUANCE AS FULLY PAID AND NON-ASSESSABLE; (2) THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE ESTABLISHED AT THE ADDRESS DESCRIBED IN THE ARTICLES, AND THE CORPORATE RECORDS DEPOSITED THEREWITH; (3) THE INDIVIDUALS DESIGNATED IN THE NOTICE OF DIRECTORS ARE CONFIRMED AS THE FIRST DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY; AND (4) THE FOLLOWING OFFICERS ARE APPOINTED, NAMELY PRESIDENT, SECRETARY, AND TREASURER, WITH FULL AUTHORITY TO OPEN BANKING ACCOUNTS, EXECUTE AGREEMENTS, AND PERFECT ALL FILINGS REQUIRED UNDER THE BUSINESS CORPORATIONS ACT (ALBERTA).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — NUANS Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name (e.g. 'X Wine & Spirits ULC') via the NUANS pre-screening portal or an authorized Alberta Registry Agent. Obtain a NUANS Corporate Name Search Report demonstrating that the name is distinguishable and reserve the name for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name for conflict or misleading use, file an amendment to the name request with a revised name; the 90-day reservation period may be renewed once.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft ULC Articles and Execute Subscriber Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Notary Public / Commissioner for Oaths (if executed outside Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) in the form prescribed by Alberta Regulation 276/2000, reflecting the ULC designation and share structure. Have all subscribers execute the Articles and each first director sign a consent. Have the execution acknowledged before a notary public if the incorporation is filed by remote/agent.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (each director)
Subscriber's due diligence records (passport, proof of address, source of funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry pre-screening finds unenforceable restrictions or missing share information, amend the Articles and re-execute before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles, Notice of Directors, and Notice of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), Form 2 (Notice of Directors), and Form 3 (Notice of Registered Office) through the Alberta Corporate Registry online filing portal or by paper at a registry agent. Pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 150.00. Retain the transaction receipt. The Certificate of Incorporation is generated electronically once the registered office and directors are accepted.
required_dossiers: NUANS report (attached if name not previously reserved)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or rejects a notice, correct the flagged items and refile within the requested reply period; no additional filing fee is charged for a registry-correction resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Federal Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After acceptance, download the official Certificate of Incorporation. Immediately complete the RC1 'Request for a Business Number' (including GST/HST account and, where required, excise duty account) through CRA's online business registration or Form RC1 mail-in. Reference the corporate registry ID and certificate number to link the provincial record.
required_dossiers: CRA Form RC1 or online registration snapshot
Corporate name search and registered office confirmation
Directors' social insurance numbers or passports for CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA delays the Business Number due to verification, contact CRA Corporate and Trust Services with the certificate copy; business may proceed under the provisional registry number only for invoicing before BN issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Initial Governance Instruments and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Alberta ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the first board resolution accepting share subscriptions and office addresses, to appoint the initial officers, to approve corporate seal (if any), and to authorize execution contracts and bank account opening. Issue share certificates to subscribers, complete the register of directors, register of shareholders, and ensure the registered office records are in place.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set forth above)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any corporate registry filing is omitted, file a voluntary late-filing correction under the ABCA; administrative penalties may apply but are waivable for inadvertent errors if disclosed promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC) — Liquor Insurance and Licensing Division; Canada Revenue Agency — Excise Duty and Licensing; Canada Border Services Agency — Commercial Licensing Unit (for bonded import storage)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Class D Liquor Wholesale/Manufacturing Licence (per AGLC Liquor Licensing Regulation); Federal Excise Warehouse Licence (Excise Act, 2001); Customs Service Provider/Warehouse Bond (CBSA bonded warehouse)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 — Exempt from full environmental impact assessment (EIA); however, an environmental site assessment and wastewater discharge registration may be required for storage or bottling activities if aggregate alcohol storage exceeds 25,000 L. For ordinary bonded redistribution, only a code-of-practice registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal wastewater discharge: biochemical oxygen demand ≤ 15 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 10 mg/L per Alberta Environment Code of Practice; VOC emissions from transfer operations must not exceed 3 tonnes per year without an approval; waste alcohol and spill residue must be collected in leak-proof bonded containers and manifested as hazardous/non-hazardous waste per Alberta hazardous waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance: NFPA/Alberta Fire Code compliance for warehouse occupancy, racking pallet high-bay storage with automatic fire suppression if storage height exceeds 3.8 m; PHYSICAL: structural load inspection certificate confirming floor loading capacity for bonded pallet racks and pallet tanks; WORKPLACE: OHS incident prevention clearance from Alberta Labour, first-aid training, and employee WHMIS certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via the My Business Account portal; customs and excise administration through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA); corporate income tax for Alberta is collected federally under the Canada–Alberta tax collection agreement; provincial alcohol licensing and bonded distribution oversight rests with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta ULC: (1) incorporate under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and obtain Alberta corporate registration documents and access number; (2) register the ULC for a CRA Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online or Form RC1/RC1A for non-resident entities, opening a corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and import/export account as applicable; (3) apply to AGLC for the required wine/spirits license and bonded warehouse or bonded transfer authorization; (4) obtain CBSA import/export program accounts for customs transactions; and (5) maintain a complete administrative file combining Alberta corporate records, CRA BN, AGLC license, and CBSA authorization for audit readiness.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under U.S. federal tax rules, the Alberta ULC may file IRS Form 8832 to make a check-the-box election, permitting classification as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity for U.S. purposes; absent the election, the ULC defaults to corporation classification. For Canadian Income Tax Act purposes no domestic check-the-box election exists, so the ULC remains a taxable corporation. Available related elections include the GST/HST closely related corporation election under section 211.1 of the Excise Tax Act, a non-resident s.216 election for Canadian rental income, periodic non-resident withholding elections on corporate distributions, and Canada–U.S. treaty tie-breaker/residency relief mechanisms. Hybrid mismatch anti-abuse rules under the Income Tax Act may recharacterize deductible payments where the ULC's U.S. check-the-box treatment creates a hybrid outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added sales tax at 5% GST in Alberta) plus federal excise duty on wine and spirits under the Excise Act, 2001; Alberta does not impose a separate provincial retail sales tax or HST, but AGLC liquor markups and licensing fees apply at the wholesale/bonded distribution stage.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, the small-supplier threshold is CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies made in Canada; non-residents making taxable supplies in the course of carrying on business in Canada are generally subject to the same threshold, with mandatory registration for persons making taxable supplies through a Canadian permanent establishment or where taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. No threshold applies for excise duty accounts, CBSA import/export program accounts, or AGLC liquor licensing, which are required regardless of revenue once bonded wine/spirits trading is conducted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping system comparable to Latin American VAT models. Registered suppliers must issue tax invoices showing the supplier's BN, invoice date, description, consideration, and GST charged, and GST/HST returns must be filed electronically once a person is registered. Customs clearance and export reporting use CBSA electronic data interchange, including eManifest and the Canadian Export Declaration system, and bonded wine/spirits removals are tracked through CBSA excise bonded warehouse records. AGLC may require electronic reporting of sales and volumes for duty/markup reconciliation, but there is no continuous transaction-control clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST zero-rating is available for supplies of goods exported from Canada and for services performed on exported movable property under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. Wine and spirits stored in a CBSA excise bonded warehouse qualify for zero-rating when removed for export and substantiated by contemporaneous shipping and payment records. Excise duty is not payable on alcohol released solely for export where the removal is made under customs control; duty-paid wine/spirits later exported can qualify for duty remission or refund under the Excise Act, 2001. The exporter must retain complete proof of export, foreign destination, ownership transfer, and actual receipt of foreign proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through CBSA's Canadian Export Reporting System
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / truck waybill showing delivery to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice, packing list, and bonded warehouse removal/transfer document
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice or SWIFT MT103 confirming foreign payment
AGLC or CBSA bonded warehouse authorization and excise removal declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST zero-rating within four years for ordinary assessments and without limitation for misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default. If export substantiation fails, the zero-rated treatment is reversed, 5% GST is assessed on the sale value, and the taxpayer is liable for unpaid tax, compounded daily arrears interest, and penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including up to 25% of the amount sought for false statements or omissions. CRA's Export Suspect Screening and CBSA verification programs apply heightened scrutiny to bonded alcohol exporters with missing or inconsistent documentation. For excise duty, fraudulent export claims can trigger administrative penalties, seizure of goods, criminal prosecution, and, for GST/HST offences, fines up to CAD 100,000 on summary conviction or up to CAD 1,000,000 on indictment plus imprisonment. Alcohol licence and bonded status can be suspended or revoked by AGLC/CBSA for non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (not a direct exchange control authority); federal banking supervision is conducted by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money laundering oversight by FINTRAC. Canada maintains no generalized foreign exchange approval regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted Article VIII obligations under the IMF and maintains full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Profit repatriation is permitted without exchange control approval, subject to withholding tax obligations under the Income Tax Act and reporting thresholds under the Currency Exchange Reporting Act. Bonded trade revenues in CAD/USD/EUR may be converted freely; no central bank authorization is required for cross-border transfers related to trade or equity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements for export receipts in Canada. Export proceeds may be held in foreign currency accounts, reinvested, or remitted freely. However, customs declarations and Canadian Export Reporting System filings must be accurate, and transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 require FINTRAC reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary collection/disbursement, but not as a substitute for a tier-1 corporate bank account. Canadian non-bank EMI / payment service providers are regulated under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), which imposes registration and risk-management obligations. However, such FIs generally cannot hold inherited or mandatory escrow funds and may not offer commercial credit or LC facilities; therefore unlicensed offshore EMIs are not viable for bonded liquor inventory settlements or statutory capital verification.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned ULC in Alberta, remote account opening is possible in principle with enhanced due diligence, but most tier-1 banks require at least one director or senior officer with signing authority to physically attend a Canadian branch or a notarized signing authority package. Alberta corporate registries require proof of authorization; if the ultimate beneficial owner is not a Canadian resident, a physical appearance (or a video-interview alternative at the bank's discretion) is generally mandated for the first signing officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ULC structure with opaque beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart, ULC incorporating documents, register of directors, Alberta Certificate of Status, valid passports of all UBOs, and a written tax characterization opinion confirming eligibility for pass-through treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded wine/spirits wholesale trade flagged as medium-risk enhanced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Federal and provincial excise licenses, bonded warehouse agreements, source-of-funds ledger, supplier/distributor contracts, and independent audit confirmation of inventory custody and goods movement from Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) bonded locations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittances sharing high AML scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-specific commercial invoices, customs entries (B3/CBSA Manifest), bills of lading, excise duty payment receipts, and a Treasury Policy document demonstrating segregation of escrowed capital and operational trade flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume SWIFT activity from an unlimited liability entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Projected cash-flow model, average value thresholds, list of counterparty banks and countries, compliance attestation with OFAC/EU/UN sanctions lists, and confirmation that no shell or bearer share arrangements exist.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and bond-escrow funds should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 clearly referencing 'Capital Contribution / Bonded Trade Escrow'. Canadian banks require the beneficiary bank, institution number, transit number, and the ULC name. No Canadian exchange control approval is necessary, but the source bank must provide a KYC/AML reference and the remitter's beneficial ownership declaration. For amounts over CAD 10,000, FINTRAC large cash transaction reporting (only for cash) and FINTRAC international electronic funds transfer reporting apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for bonded Scotch and Bordeaux inventory should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers, MT700/MT707 for documentary/commercial letters of credit, and LVTS (Large Value Transfer System) for domestic CAD clearing. Correspondent banks in the UK and France may be used for GBP/EUR disbursements. All outbound transfers must include settlement instructions compliant with the International Chamber of Commerce UCP600 rules for LCs and the Uniform Rules for Demand Guarantees (URDG 758) where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP forward contracts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with transfer restrictions (only as a secondary tool, subject to bank counterparty credit threshold)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD-EUR, CAD-GBP) for matching bonded trade receivables and payables
Vanilla FX options on CAD/GBP and CAD/EUR for protection on large vintage inventory purchase orders
FX swap contracts for temporary liquidity bridging between bonded warehouse release and wholesale settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No initial monetary penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution or strike-off. Reinstatement requires filing back returns and paying applicable reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failures may add an additional 10% penalty. Interest accrues on unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the annual GST/HST reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or remit attracts arrears interest and late-filing penalties; gross negligence and wilful default penalties may apply under the Excise Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit threshold applies to a private Alberta ULC. An auditor is not required if all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment. A shareholder or meeting requisition may compel an audit under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Bonded liquor and wine licensing authorities may require audited or reviewed financial statements as a licensing condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the commonly used framework for private Alberta ULCs; IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and may be adopted voluntarily. Books and records must support the Income Tax Act and customs/excise bonding requirements where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, before filing the Alberta Corporate Annual Return, the ULC must reconcile the Register of Members, record all share transfers with dated entries, and confirm each individual with significant control (25% or more of shares or control rights) remains accurately identified. Ownership changes during the year must be recorded in the registers, and non-resident shareholding percentages must be updated for federal and provincial compliance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined statutory headline rate (15% Canada federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No discretionary tax holiday applies in Canada or Alberta. The Alberta ULC is taxable as a Canadian federal/provincial corporation. Preferential effective rates arise only where the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC): federal small business rate of 9% and Alberta small business rate of 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. Additional relief includes the capital dividend account for non-taxable capital gains, investment tax credits, scientific research and experimental development credits, and accelerated capital cost allowance. Bonded warehouse excise taxes and GST/HST are not income taxes and do not reduce federal/provincial income tax rates.
